To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

there are four segments of Spanish consumers according to their level and type of socially responsibility consumption: highly responsible, moderately responsible, sensitive to the origin of products, and indifferent.

consumers can be classified into four different segments based on their socially responsible consumption, with the highly responsible and sensitive to origin segments being the most relevant for the development of effective campaigns.

the individuals who are most likely and most willing to act in favor of socially responsible consumption are those who are emotionally engaged with these problems and perceive that they can make a difference.
In summary, our research is concerned with
identifying segments of consumers with different levels of socially responsible behavior, and with analyzing the attitudes that determine this behavior.
the development of new strategies for promoting socially responsible consumption, based on the emotional involvement of individuals and their belief that their actions can make a difference.
the identification of the profiles of Spanish consumers with respect to the degree and type of social responsibility.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the individuals from the segments of consumers with a high level of socially responsible behavior have more favorable attitudes and are more emotionally engaged than those from the segments with lower levels of socially responsible behavior.

, in order to design campaigns to promote socially responsibility, it is necessary to focus on emotional engagement, as well as on personal effectiveness, as they are the variables that are most relevant to consumers.

the individuals from each segment are differentiated from the other ones because they have different levels of engagement with the problems and different levels of perceived personal effectiveness in relation to the problems.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the individuals who are most likely and most willing to act responsibly are those who feel personally involved with the problems of humanity and who believe that their actions have an impact on them.
, in order to promote socially responsible behavior, it is necessary to work on emotional engagement, and on the perception of personal efficacy, but not on personal gain.

, in general terms, the most responsible consumers are those who have a greater sense of responsibility, who feel more emotionally involved in the environmental and social problem, and who feel more effective in the face of this situation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
socially responsible consumers do not differ from other consumers in terms of sociodemographic characteristics; instead, they differ in their attitude towards the problems.
the promotion of socially responsible consumption must be directed to the individual's attitudes, not to their sociodemographics, in order to be effective.
it is possible to identify segments that can be targeted with campaigns to promote socially-responsible consumption.
